shape.token_to_canonical_DIRECTION_FLAG: REAL GAP, not a rename — flagging for human decision. The doc says the frontmatter parser resolves a `tools:` token (e.g. 'Bash') to a canonical id via a lookup 'WHERE platform_tool_name = token AND platform = claude_code -> canonical tool id'. The ONLY resolution method BindingStore actually ships is `resolve(canonicalToolName, platformId): string` (binding-store.ts:194-214), which goes the OPPOSITE direction: canonical -> platform alias, returning `platformToolName`. There is NO shipped method that takes a platform alias and returns the canonical tool name. Verified by grepping the whole package for any reverse-lookup method — none exists; `listForPlatform(platformId): ToolPlatformBinding[]` (binding-store.ts:220-234) is the only method that returns the full binding set, requiring the caller to filter client-side (`bindings.find(b => b.platformToolName === token)` then take `b.toolName`). RECOMMENDATION for the frontmatter-parser/import-pipeline states: either (a) add a `BindingStore.resolveCanonical(platformToolName, platformId)` method upstream to @adhd/agent-store-tools before this plan depends on it, or (b) have the migration's own frontmatter parser call `listForPlatform('claude_code')` once, build a local Map<platformToolName, toolName>, and do the lookup client-side, flagging any token with no match (same never-silently-dropped behavior as originally documented).

The stale doc's importAgent flow ('writes AgentToolStore grants for the resolved canonical tool ids') never specifies what permission level an imported agent's frontmatter `tools:` grant should receive — this must be decided (e.g. always 'full', or derived from a frontmatter field) before the import-pipeline state can call grant() correctly.
